**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, §3.4 Termination for Convenience).**

What I found:
- **§3.4** — Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for convenience at the end of any calendar month on one month's written notice. That beats the fallback (60–90 days) and matches the preferred 30-day position.
- **No Vendor convenience right** — §3.3 is mutual for-cause with a 30-day cure (7 business days for Customer nonpayment), and §3.3 expressly bars IBM from recovering §3.4(b) early termination charges where IBM is the breaching party (favourable to us). §3.2 is end-of-term non-renewal on 90 days' notice, and §13.1 gives Customer an extra exit if IBM changes the Services. Nothing lets IBM walk mid-term for convenience.
- **The gap** — §3.4(b) makes our exit contingent on uncapped "early termination charges... specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments," and §3.5 provides no refund of prepaid Charges (it only accelerates accrued amounts). An open-ended exit penalty fails the fallback ceiling of three months' fees.

Redline (validated, ok:true) — minimal edit to §3.4(b) capping early termination charges at three months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services and adding a refund of prepaid Charges for the post-termination period, leaving the one-month notice and Attachment A mechanic untouched.
